newsitem.title: SPAIN: INSTANT VIEW -- Spain inflation falls to 1.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- Spain inflation falls to 1.7 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from economists after Spanish inflation fell to a lower-than-expected 1.7 percent year on year in April from 2.2 percent in March.
Economists had expected inflation to fall to 1.9 percent.
MARCO PIANELLI, ECONOMIST AT NOMURA, LONDON

"It's a good number...core (which fell to 1.9 percent versus 2.1 percent in March) in particular was promising...The Bank of Spain will cut rates by a quarter of a point, which will be supportive of the market. But this is already priced in."
FRANCESCO GIORDANO, ECONOMIST AT CSFB IN LONDON

"The April CPI is very good. It's better than expected and the overall picture is very, very positive. Even if you consider that service prices are more resilient and food prices are expected to invert their positive trend in the summer, Spanish inflation remains very good.
On a quarterly basis, and seasonally-adjusted, a measure that other central banks refer to, Spanish inflation is below 1.0 percent.

"Despite this, and despite more optimism over rates in Europe, I do not think this good number will open the doors to a 50 basis points cut by the Bank of Spain because the economy is picking up. Consumer confidence is recovering and so I do not think they will need to be more aggressive in monetary easing.
VALENTIN FERNANDEZ, ECONOMIST AT CREDIT LYONNAIS IN MADRID
"This number is very good, better than expected. Now we have a 99 percent probability that the Bank of Spain will cut the official rate at its repo on Friday.

"Now it seems to me the real question is not when, but how much, because it is also possibile to cut more than 25 basis points. But I'm still thinking they will cut by 25 basis points. In this way, they will leave themselves scope for another rate cut before the summer, and the peseta can improve from here.
"In May inflation can fall from here, to around 1.6 percent or even more.
